rules.text: Check the simplest things first: power, cables, buttons, then a restart. Don't start by taking things apart.
Gather symptoms: when it started, what changed before, and whether it can be repeated.
Trust evidence (error messages, indicator lights, system readings), not guesses or rumors.
FIX when something is wrong or broken but can be sorted out without a new part: reseat, clean, or reset it.
ESCALATE when it needs permission or access that Workshop technicians don't have (restricted folders, servers, licenses). Don't look for shortcuts.
If the device is healthy and the problem is how it's used or a simple setting, GUIDE THE USER. Don't take anything apart.
Explain the steps one at a time in simple words, then make sure the user can repeat them alone.
Technicians never ask for a user's password. Forgot the password? Point them to the official reset page.
Write the cause and the fix in the ticket, so similar problems get solved faster.
REPLACE A PART only when the evidence shows physical damage: cracked, burnt, swollen, clicking, or failing tests.
Parts that are loose, dirty, or dusty just need FIXING: reseat or clean them, then test again.
A swollen battery can catch fire: don't charge it, don't press it, replace it right away.
Shut down and unplug the power before opening the case. Touch metal or wear an antistatic strap.
Check from nearest to farthest: cable or Wi-Fi, IP address, router (gateway), internet, then DNS.
An IP address of 169.254.x.x means the device didn't get an address from the router (DHCP failed).
Can ping an IP address but website names won't open? That's a DNS problem, not a dead internet.
If many people or a whole floor drop at once, the problem is in the central network: ESCALATE to the network team.
A nearly full disk (above 90%) makes the computer slow. Clear temporary files and move big files.
Install official security updates regularly. Updates put off for months are a security hole.
Problem started right after a driver update? Roll the driver back to the previous version.
Install apps only from the company App Portal, not from websites or files people send.
ESCALATE when it needs special access or expertise (servers, licenses, data recovery). Write down what you've tried.
Signs of an attack (unknown programs, antivirus turning itself off, locked files, cursor moving by itself): disconnect the network and escalate to the SOC team.
Don't experiment with important data on a dying disk. Escalate to the data recovery team before anything is replaced.
Burning smell, smoke, or spilled liquid: unplug the power first and don't switch it on again.
